study_area.name: Whole study area

detected_change.what: Water extent decreased: 495.2 ha of water became land (0.0 ha became water).

hypotheses.title: Reservoir water-level decline exposed shoreline

evidence.statement: Water loss (495.2 ha) dominates water gain (0.0 ha): the water edge retreated.
57% of loss patches attached to land that stayed dry: partly shoreline-attached.
HV polarisation shows no usable water/land separation in these scenes (water sits near the noise floor), so HV can neither confirm nor contradict the HH result.

Sentinel-2 (independent optical sensor): 28% of NISAR water-loss pixels lie within 40 m of shoreline that also changed from water to land optically (2026-07-03 to 2026-10-11). Pixel-exact, 30% are dry land in the same-day optical image (exact matching is unreliable for 1-3 pixel bands).
Optical water extent changed from 54247.3 ha (2026-07-03) to 53383.7 ha (2026-10-11), -863.6 ha. It was stable between 2026-06-13 (54184.2 ha) and 2026-07-03, which bracket the first radar date.
4 of 4 sectors with significant change show the same direction - a reservoir-wide pattern, as a level change would produce.
No in-situ gauge or satellite-altimetry water level for these dates was available to the pipeline.

hypotheses.note: A water-level change is a description of what happened, not of why; it does not identify the operator decision, inflow, or withdrawal behind it.
hypotheses.reason: Insufficient evidence because the available evidence is too weak or conflicting to rank it higher. Evidence lines: supporting 3 (NISAR HH, NISAR HH (all sectors), Sentinel-2 L2A (extent)); contradicting 1 (Sentinel-2 L2A (co-location)); missing 2.

hypotheses.title: Seasonal water-level variation

evidence.statement: Only two NISAR observations (2026-06-25 and 2026-10-11): a seasonal cycle cannot be resolved from one pair.
Between the dates, reference evapotranspiration (589.2 mm) was 3.5x precipitation (167.8 mm) at the reservoir: a warm-season water deficit, consistent with seasonal drawdown.
No multi-year water-level or satellite record for Mingachevir was available to compare 2026 against typical years.

As a result, the current findings currently suggest insufficient evidence regarding the situation.
